rag.name: Finset.prod_sdiff_eq_prod_sdiff_iff
rag.content:
@[to_additive]
lemma prod_sdiff_eq_prod_sdiff_iff :
    ∏ i ∈ s \ t, f i = ∏ i ∈ t \ s, f i ↔ ∏ i ∈ s, f i = ∏ i ∈ t, f i :=
  eq_comm.trans <| eq_iff_eq_of_mul_eq_mul <| by
    rw [← prod_union disjoint_sdiff_self_left, ← prod_union disjoint_sdiff_self_left,
      sdiff_union_self_eq_union, sdiff_union_self_eq_union, union_comm]

rag.name: Finset.prod_sdiff_div_prod_sdiff
rag.content:
@[to_additive]
theorem prod_sdiff_div_prod_sdiff :
    (∏ x ∈ s₂ \ s₁, f x) / ∏ x ∈ s₁ \ s₂, f x = (∏ x ∈ s₂, f x) / ∏ x ∈ s₁, f x := by
  simp [← Finset.prod_sdiff (@inf_le_left _ _ s₁ s₂), ← Finset.prod_sdiff (@inf_le_right _ _ s₁ s₂)]

lemma measure_symmDiff_eq (hs : NullMeasurableSet s μ) (ht : NullMeasurableSet t μ) :
    μ (s ∆ t) = μ (s \ t) + μ (t \ s) := by
  simpa only [symmDiff_def, sup_eq_union]
    using measure_union₀ (ht.diff hs) disjoint_sdiff_sdiff.aedisjoint

rag.content:

  Nat.add_right_cancel (m := #t) <| by
    simp_rw [card_sdiff_add_card, ← h, card_sdiff_add_card, union_comm]

informal_statement: For any two sets \( X_1 \) and \( X_2 \), the set \( C \) has the form of the symmetric difference of \( X_1 \) and \( X_2 \). In other words, \( C = (X_1 \cup X_2) \setminus (X_1 \cap X_2) \).
informal_proof: The set \( C \) is defined as the symmetric difference of \( X_1 \) and \( X_2 \), which consists of elements that are in either \( X_1 \) or \( X_2 \) but not in both. By the definition of symmetric difference, this equality holds as a fundamental property of set operations. Thus, \( C = (X_1 \cup X_2) \setminus (X_1 \cap X_2) \).
